positive_examples._comment: NORM_DIRECT: A fundamental implementation choice not tied to any CSR field
positive_examples.input_excerpt: Implementations may implement zero, 16, or 64 PMP entries; the lowest-numbered PMP entries must be implemented first. All PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.

expected_output.excerpt: Implementations may implement zero, 16, or 64 PMP entries; the lowest-numbered PMP entries must be implemented first.
expected_output.reasoning: The number of PMP entries is a direct implementation choice (0, 16, or 64). It is not controlled by any CSR field.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_DIRECT: A vector extension parameter defined at implementation time
positive_examples.input_excerpt:
. The maximum size in bits of a vector element that any operation can produce or consume, _ELEN_ >= 8, which must be a power of 2.
. The number of bits in a single vector register, _VLEN_ >= ELEN, which must be a power of 2, and must be no greater than 2^16.

expected_output.excerpt: The maximum size in bits of a vector element that any operation can produce or consume, _ELEN_ >= 8, which must be a power of 2.
expected_output.reasoning: ELEN is a direct implementation parameter: the maximum element size. It has constraints (>= 8, power of 2) but the specific value is chosen by the implementer.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_CSR_WARL: The legal values of a WARL CSR field
positive_examples.input_excerpt:
The `mtvec` register is an MXLEN-bit WARL read/write register that holds trap vector configuration, consisting of a vector base address (BASE) and a vector mode (MODE).
...
The `mtvec` register must always be implemented, but can contain a read-only value. If `mtvec` is writable, the set of values the register may hold can vary by implementation.

expected_output.excerpt: If `mtvec` is writable, the set of values the register may hold can vary by implementation.
expected_output.reasoning: The mtvec MODE field is WARL, and the set of supported mode values (Direct=0, Vectored=1) varies by implementation. The parameter is the set of legal MODE values.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_CSR_RW: Controls whether CSR fields are read-only or read-write
positive_examples.input_excerpt:
The MBE, SBE, and UBE bits in `mstatus` and `mstatush` are WARL fields that control the endianness of memory accesses other than instruction fetches.
...
If S-mode is supported, an implementation may make SBE be a read-only copy of MBE.

expected_output.excerpt: The MBE, SBE, and UBE bits in `mstatus` and `mstatush` are WARL fields that control the endianness of memory accesses other than instruction fetches.
expected_output.reasoning: The implementation chooses whether MBE is read-only-0 (always little-endian), read-only-1 (always big-endian), or read-write (dynamic endianness). This controls the RO/RW nature of the field, not just which values are legal.

positive_examples._comment: SW_RULE: Implementation-defined but deterministic with correct software
positive_examples.input_excerpt: If an instruction explicitly or implicitly writes a floating-point register or the `fcsr` but does not alter its contents, and FS=Initial or FS=Clean, it is implementation-defined whether FS transitions to Dirty.

expected_output.excerpt: it is implementation-defined whether FS transitions to Dirty.
expected_output.reasoning: Whether hardware updates mstatus.FS to Dirty is implementation-defined, but software can handle this deterministically by checking and managing FS state with proper fencing. The outcome is predictable if software follows the rules.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_CSR_RW: Whether a CSR is read-only or read-write
positive_examples.input_excerpt: The `mtvec` register must always be implemented, but can contain a read-only value.

expected_output.excerpt: The `mtvec` register must always be implemented, but can contain a read-only value.
expected_output.reasoning: The implementation chooses whether mtvec is read-only or read-write. This is a binary choice about the mutability of the register.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_CSR_RW: Counter-inhibit bits — which HPM counters are implemented
positive_examples.input_excerpt: The counter-inhibit register `mcountinhibit` is a 32-bit WARL register that controls which of the hardware performance-monitoring counters increment.

expected_output.excerpt: The counter-inhibit register `mcountinhibit` is a 32-bit WARL register that controls which of the hardware performance-monitoring counters increment.
expected_output.reasoning: Which bits of mcountinhibit are writable depends on which HPM counters are implemented. Unimplemented counters have read-only-zero bits. This is a NORM_CSR_RW parameter because it determines which bits of the WARL register are functional.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_CSR_WARL: VM translation mode support in hgatp
positive_examples.input_excerpt: A write to `hgatp` with an unsupported MODE value is not ignored as it is for `satp`. Instead, the fields of `hgatp` are WARL in the normal way, so an unsupported value is simply not stored.

expected_output.excerpt: the fields of `hgatp` are WARL in the normal way, so an unsupported value is simply not stored.
expected_output.reasoning: Whether the Bare mode is a legal value in hgatp.MODE is an implementation choice. The hgatp fields are WARL, so unsupported MODE values are not stored. The parameter is whether Bare is in the set of supported modes.

positive_examples._comment: NORM_DIRECT: tval reporting — what value is written on exception
positive_examples.input_excerpt: The `mtval` register can optionally also be used to return the faulting instruction bits on an illegal-instruction exception (`mepc` points to the faulting instruction in memory). If `mtval` is written with a nonzero value, then `mtval` will contain either the faulting portion of the instruction or all the bytes of the faulting instruction.

expected_output.excerpt: The `mtval` register can optionally also be used to return the faulting instruction bits on an illegal-instruction exception.
expected_output.reasoning: Whether mtval reports the faulting instruction encoding on an illegal-instruction exception is optional — the implementation chooses. This is NORM_DIRECT because no CSR field controls this choice; it is a design-time decision.

positive_examples.input_excerpt: An SC can only pair with the most recent LR in program order. An SC may succeed only if no store from another hart to the reservation set can be observed to have occurred between the LR and the SC, and if there is no other SC between the LR and the SC in program order.

expected_output.excerpt: An SC may succeed only if no store from another hart to the reservation set can be observed to have occurred between the LR and the SC.
expected_output.reasoning: Whether SC fails when the address does not exactly match the LR is implementation-defined. The spec says SC 'may succeed' under certain conditions, implying the implementation chooses the exact failure policy.

negative_examples._comment: FALSE POSITIVE: NOTE block discussing implementation options — non-normative
negative_examples.input_excerpt:
[NOTE]
====
Some platforms may choose to disallow speculatively writing FS to close a potential side channel.
====
negative_examples.reason_for_rejection: This text is inside a [NOTE] block and is therefore non-normative. It describes a platform suggestion, not an architectural requirement. Do not extract parameters from NOTE, TIP, WARNING, or IMPORTANT blocks.

negative_examples._comment: FALSE POSITIVE: Behavior controlled by a CSR field value, not a parameter itself
negative_examples.input_excerpt: When MODE=Direct, all traps into machine mode cause the `pc` to be set to the address in the BASE field.
negative_examples.reason_for_rejection: This describes what happens when mtvec.MODE has a specific value. The behavior is determined by the CSR field value at runtime, not by an implementation choice. The parameter is which MODE values are supported (MTVEC_MODES), not this behavioral description.

negative_examples._comment: FALSE POSITIVE: Fixed architectural requirement, not an implementation choice
negative_examples.input_excerpt: This register must be readable in any implementation.
negative_examples.reason_for_rejection: This is a fixed requirement ('must be readable') that all implementations must satisfy. There is no implementation choice here — it is not a parameter.

negative_examples._comment: FALSE POSITIVE: 'may' used as permission/capability, not as optionality
negative_examples.input_excerpt: Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to `pmp0cfg`, then writing all ones to `pmpaddr0`, then reading back `pmpaddr0`.
negative_examples.reason_for_rejection: Here 'may' means 'is allowed to' (permission), not 'might or might not' (optionality). This describes a software technique, not an implementation-defined parameter.
